convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom for the MaByMa indicator and depends on two external .mqh libraries (TradeAlgorithms.mqh, SmoothAlgorithms.mqh) for trade execution and smoothing algorithms. Custom indicator with non-standard smoothing methods (JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) requires manual recreation.

derived_values.name: min_rates_total - minimum bars needed for indicator warmup
TimeShiftSec - timeframe duration in seconds
derived_values.used_by: UpSignalTime and DnSignalTime calculation for position open timing

other_exits: BuyPosClose and SellPosClose are enabled by default via BuyPosClose/SellPosClose input booleans; opposite signal triggers close of existing position

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MM=0.1 is interpreted based on MMMode: when MMMode=LOT it is fixed lots (0.1 lots); when MMMode=FREEMARGIN/BALANCE/LOSSFREEMARGIN/LOSSBALANCE it is a fraction of the respective margin base

custom_logic_notes: Entry uses a two-bar crossover: Ind[1]>Sign[1] (previous bar indicator above signal) AND Ind[0]<=Sign[0] (current bar indicator at or below signal) triggers BUY_Open - this is a crossover where the indicator was above signal on the previous bar and crossed to or below on the current bar. The SignalBar input (default=1) shifts which bar is used for the 'previous' vs 'current' comparison. When SignalBar=0, the EA recalculates on every tick instead of only on new bars. The UpSignalTime/DnSignalTime is set to the last bar date + one timeframe period, effectively marking the next bar open time. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose functions with built-in position management and GlobalVariableDel_ cleanup.
python_conversion_notes: The MaByMa custom indicator must be reimplemented in Python. It applies a smoothing algorithm (MA_Method1) to price, then applies a second smoothing algorithm (MA_Method2) to the result. The SmoothAlgorithms.mqh library implements 10 smoothing methods (SMA, EMA, SMMA, LWMA, JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) - JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA are non-standard and require porting from the .mqh source. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh must also be ported for position sizing (5 margin modes) and order execution helpers. The crossover logic is inverted from typical: a buy signal occurs when Ind[1]>Sign[1] AND Ind[0]<=Sign[0], meaning the indicator was above and crossed down - this is actually a bearish crossover triggering a buy, which may be intentional (mean reversion) or a quirk of the MaByMa indicator interpretation. SL/TP are in points (not pips), so for 5-digit brokers 1000 points = 100 pips; no digit adjustment code is present in the EA itself. The GetStartBars function from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh must also be ported to calculate proper warmup periods.
